Former Cheltenham Town Women's Captain Emily Owen Departs, Citing 'Psychological Unsafe' Environment

04 Nov 2026, 08:34 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.bbc.com

Departure After Four Years

Emily Owen has announced her departure from Cheltenham Town's women's team after spending four years with the club and making over 130 appearances. The defender played in the Women's National League Southern Premier. Her exit became public after the club shared news of her departure on social media on Monday.

Following the club's announcement, Owen released her own statement to clarify the reasons behind her leaving, stating she wanted to address rumours circulating about her exit.

Allegations of a 'Dictatorship'

In her public statement, Owen alleged that the club had been turned into a dictatorship by "an individual" who she claimed held "far too much control within this team." She stated that this environment left players feeling "psychologically unsafe."

Additionally, Owen claimed that:

  • Three other players had also left the club on moral grounds.
  • Boundaries were crossed that "shouldn't be crossed in women's football."
  • Her departure was prompted by "a lack of an individual's principles and outright failures in processes."

Club Response

In response to the claims, a spokesperson for Cheltenham Town Women stated that the club does not comment on individual cases. However, the organization emphasized that it takes player welfare and wellbeing "extremely seriously."

The club's official statement added:

  • Cheltenham Town Women are committed to ensuring every player, staff member, and volunteer is treated with respect.
  • The club aims to maintain an environment where individuals feel safe, valued, and supported.
  • Any concerns brought to the club's attention will be handled appropriately, sensitively, and in accordance with all relevant policies and procedures.

How to Verify

Readers seeking to verify official club statements or follow future updates regarding Cheltenham Town Women can consult the club's official website and verified social media channels, or refer to reports from established sports news outlets such as the BBC.
